guide.title: Ostia Lido, Rome: Q. XXXIII at the mouth of the Tiber, its two towers and the seaplane base
guide.intro: Ostia Lido in the strict sense is Q. XXXIII, whose full name is Lido di Ostia Ponente, also known as Ostia Ponente or Nuova Ostia. It is the thirty-third quartiere of Rome, one of the three quartieri that make up Ostia, and third from last in the official series. It is the western third of the settlement, at the mouth of the Tiber, and the seafront that the name Ostia calls to mind is not in it: the pier, piazza Anco Marzio, the bathing establishments, the pinewood and both railway stations stand in Q. XXXIV Lido di Ostia Levante or in Q. XXXV Lido di Castel Fusano. What Q. XXXIII holds instead is two coastal towers, a disused seaplane base with a marina and a bird reserve laid out over it, and an inland strip of 1920s and 1930s civic architecture along corso Duca di Genova and via Ostiense.

sections.heading: What Q. XXXIII holds, and what belongs to its neighbours
sections.body:
The quartiere sets out its own edges, and they matter here more than usual, because the whole settlement reads as one town and every source says simply Ostia. To the north-west it meets the comune di Fiumicino, separated by the Tiber from the river mouth to the ponte di Tor Boacciana. To the north-east it meets the zona Z. XXXV Ostia Antica, separated by via di Tor Boacciana and via Guido Calza as far as via Ostiense. To the east it meets the zona Z. XXXIV Casal Palocco along via Ostiense, and then the quartiere Q. XXXIV Lido di Ostia Levante, separated by via Ostiense, viale Capitan Consalvo and viale della Marina as far as the rotonda at piazza dei Ravennati. To the south-west is the Tyrrhenian Sea, from that rotonda to the Tiber mouth.

The practical consequence is that a run of famous names falls outside the quartiere. The Pontile di Ostia, piazza Anco Marzio and piazza dei Ravennati, the Palazzo del Governatorato that seats Municipio X, the Villini Rossini, the church of Santa Maria Regina Pacis, the Borghetto dei Pescatori and the stations of Lido di Ostia Centro and Lido di Ostia Nord are all in Q. XXXIV Levante. The Pineta di Castel Fusano, the Villa della Palombara, piazzale Cristoforo Colombo with its Fontana dello Zodiaco, and the Kursaal and Vecchia Pineta bathing establishments are in Q. XXXV Lido di Castel Fusano. The excavated Roman city, the Museo Ostiense, the Castello di Giulio II and Borgo Gregoriopoli belong to the zona Z. XXXV Ostia Antica. Note the numeral trap while you are here: Q. XXXV is Lido di Castel Fusano and Z. XXXV is Ostia Antica, and they are two different units.

The quartiere was created by delibera 2453 of 13 September 1961, signed by the Commissario Straordinario Francesco Diana, which split the older Lido di Ostia quartiere in three; that older unit was officially instituted in 1940 and had existed since May 1933. Q. XXXIII lies in Municipio Roma X, and the zona urbanistica 13F Ostia Nord extends across its territory. One further body of coast has its own legal existence: the Riserva naturale statale Litorale Romano, a state nature reserve constituted by ministerial decree, covering 16,327 hectares across the comuni of Roma and Fiumicino, jointly managed by the two comuni and carrying the identifier EUAP0086.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body:
The Metromare, the former ferrovia Roma-Lido, runs from Rome to Ostia; the line reached Ostia Lido in 1924. The two stations named on this quartiere's own transport list, Lido di Ostia Nord and Lido di Ostia Centro, are placed by their own articles inside Q. XXXIV Lido di Ostia Levante. Steer by addresses instead.

Three addresses cover the river mouth. Via dell'Idroscalo is the access road for the site of the seaplane base, for the Centro Habitat Mediterraneo and for the Parco Letterario Pier Paolo Pasolini; LIPU gives the oasis as Via dell'Idroscalo, 00121 Lido di Ostia RM. Tor San Michele stands in a green area between via degli Atlantici and via dell'Idroscalo. Tor Boacciana is on via del Ponte di Tor Boacciana, about four kilometres from the river mouth. The marina is at Lungomare Duca degli Abruzzi 84, 00121, with a vehicle entrance from via del Porto di Roma, and the Biblioteca Elsa Morante is at that same address for the time being.

The inland strip runs on corso Duca di Genova and via Ostiense. The Ufficio postale is on piazzale della Posta at the corner of the two; the Palazzo dell'ex GIL is at Corso Duca di Genova 82, with a second frontage at via delle Sirene 79; the Scuola Fratelli Garrone is on corso Duca di Genova as well; the Teatro del Lido is at Via delle Sirene 22, inside the ex Colonia marina block off lungomare Paolo Toscanelli. Cineland is out at Viale dei Romagnoli 515, its facade turned toward the via del Mare.

Arriving by sea is a real option here. The Porto Turistico di Roma states that its berths take vessels from 8 to 60 metres, that its control tower works VHF channel 74 between 07.00 and 23.00, and that boats up to 20 metres staying at most two nights need no booking and should call the tower on that channel.

sections.heading: Opening hours and access
sections.body:
Three places here publish their own hours. LIPU states that the visitor centre of the Centro Habitat Mediterraneo opens on Mondays, Wednesdays, Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays from 10.00 to 13.00 for information and for wildlife rescue; that on Saturdays and Sundays from 10.00 to 13.00 there is free access to the oasis; and that guided visits are possible on any day of the week if booked in advance. Biblioteche di Roma gives the Biblioteca Elsa Morante, at its substitute address in the Porto Turistico, as open Monday to Friday 09.00 to 19.00 and Saturday 09.00 to 13.00, closed on Sundays, for 2 January to 31 December 2026, with the telephone number 06 45460481. The Porto Turistico gives its office hours as 09.00 to 13.00 and 15.00 to 19.00, and its control tower as working VHF 74 from 07.00 to 23.00.

Tor San Michele is owned by the Soprintendenza Speciale Archeologia Belle Arti e Paesaggio di Roma, which tendered its management; the tender was won in 2018 by the Associazione Culturale Quattro Sassi, which reopened the tower during 2021, and the tower's own article records that it can be visited by booking. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here. The same is true of Tor Boacciana, of the church of Santa Monica, and of the post office on piazzale della Posta, which is a working post office rather than a museum.

Two buildings cannot be entered at all. The Palazzo dell'ex GIL has stood empty since the school inside it closed in July 2009. The Scuola Fratelli Garrone is a working primary school, a secondary site of the Istituto Comprensivo Via Giuliano da Sangallo, and no public access is published for it; it is a building to look at from the street. The Teatro del Lido publishes its season through Roma Capitale's Teatri in Comune circuit rather than a standing timetable, and Cineland publishes its programme and ticketing on its own site.

faq.question: Is this Rome's beach?
faq.answer: Not the part of it people mean. Q. XXXIII Lido di Ostia Ponente is the western third of Ostia, at the mouth of the Tiber. The historic seafront belongs to its neighbours: the Pontile di Ostia, piazza Anco Marzio and the Palazzo del Governatorato are in Q. XXXIV Lido di Ostia Levante, and the pinewood, piazzale Cristoforo Colombo and the Kursaal and Vecchia Pineta bathing establishments are in Q. XXXV Lido di Castel Fusano. What Q. XXXIII gives a visitor is the river mouth, two coastal towers, a bird reserve and marina on the site of a seaplane base, and a strip of 1920s and 1930s civic architecture inland.

faq.question: Which railway station serves this quartiere?
faq.answer: The Metromare, the former ferrovia Roma-Lido, runs from Rome to Ostia and reached Ostia Lido in 1924. The quartiere's own transport list names Lido di Ostia Nord and Lido di Ostia Centro, but both stations' own articles place them inside Q. XXXIV Lido di Ostia Levante. Navigate by street addresses: via dell'Idroscalo for the river mouth, corso Duca di Genova and via Ostiense for the inland strip, Lungomare Duca degli Abruzzi 84 for the marina and the library.

faq.question: Can Tor San Michele be visited?
faq.answer: Its own article records that it can be visited by booking. The tower belongs to the Soprintendenza Speciale Archeologia Belle Arti e Paesaggio di Roma, which took it over in 1994 and opened it exceptionally on 28 May 2017; the Soprintendenza then tendered its management, and the Associazione Culturale Quattro Sassi won the tender in 2018 and reopened the tower during 2021. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.

faq.question: Where is the Biblioteca Elsa Morante at the moment?
faq.answer: Its normal home is inside the ex Colonia marina on lungomare Paolo Toscanelli, but it has been working from a substitute address since September 2025 while energy-efficiency works are carried out. Biblioteche di Roma prints that substitute address as Porto Turistico di Roma, Lungomare Duca degli Abruzzi 84, 00121 Roma, telephone 06 45460481, and gives hours for 2 January to 31 December 2026 of Monday to Friday 09.00 to 19.00 and Saturday 09.00 to 13.00, closed Sunday. The Fondo Ostia, its collection on the history and the natural and urban landscape of the Roman coast, is not on open shelves and has to be asked for at the desk.

faq.question: What is left of the Idroscalo?
faq.answer: The seaplane base itself is gone: German forces destroyed the main structures in 1943, and what survived was absorbed into later works. The site is now shared by three things: the Porto Turistico di Roma, the Centro Habitat Mediterraneo run by LIPU, and the Parco Letterario Pier Paolo Pasolini on the place where Pasolini was killed in 1975. Tor San Michele, which the base enclosed in 1928 and used as a radio beacon, still stands between via degli Atlantici and via dell'Idroscalo. Turismo Roma records that the landscape is still marked by the bilancioni, the lift nets used for eel fishing.

faq.question: Is Tor Boacciana part of the Ostia Antica excavations?
faq.answer: No. The tower stands on the bank of the Tiber in this quartiere, on via del Ponte di Tor Boacciana, and the quartiere's own article names it among its military structures. it.wikipedia records that it is managed by the Parco archeologico di Ostia antica, which is a statement about who runs it. The excavated Roman city and the Museo Ostiense are in the zona Z. XXXV Ostia Antica, a separate unit.

places.name: Tor San Michele
places.summary: An octagonal coastal fort in the eastern part of a wide green area between via degli Atlantici and via dell'Idroscalo. It stands about a hundred metres from the river and roughly two kilometres from the sea; it.wikipedia records that it was originally 50 metres from the shoreline. Roma Capitale gives the octagonal building a height of 18 metres and a perimeter of 96; it.wikipedia gives 24.1 metres overall, of which 18.5 is the tower and 5.6 the off-centre lantern turret, with sides of about 12 metres. It is casemated throughout on three levels, each of eight cross-vaulted rooms, and was ringed by a moat with a double drawbridge system; the sloping terrace carries a circular opening eight metres across under a corbelled cornice. The building belongs to the Soprintendenza Speciale Archeologia Belle Arti e Paesaggio di Roma, and its own article records that it can be visited by booking. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.
places.history: The Tiber flood of 15 September 1557 shifted the river northward and pushed the coast near the delta forward by more than a kilometre, and the tower belongs to the review of the coastal defences that Pius IV then entrusted to Francesco Laparelli. It was built on a design attributed to Michelangelo Buonarroti; the building's own article records that the attribution has never been established. Roma Capitale gives the work as begun in 1559 and finished in 1568, under Pius V, by Giovanni Lippi. it.wikipedia, citing Colonna 2013, instead has Nanni di Baccio Bigio taking over on Michelangelo's death in 1564 and, on his own death in August 1568, his son Alessandro completing the work in 1569. The two accounts are not reconciled here. Pius V consecrated the finished tower to Michael the Archangel, the saint whose name he had taken on entering the Dominicans. In August 1589 Saracen vessels passed it because its artillery was in poor condition, and a 1592 inventory in the Archivio di Stato di Roma lists half a culverin, a falcon and a falconet, five arquebuses, powder, and iron and lead shot. With the opening of the Ostia seaplane base in 1928 the tower fell inside its perimeter and served as a radio beacon; windows were cut in the outer walls in 1930. In the Second World War it was used by Italian and German forces and later by Allied ones. It was consigned to the Soprintendenza in 1994, opened exceptionally on 28 May 2017, and reopened during 2021 by the Associazione Culturale Quattro Sassi, which had won the management tender in 2018.

places.name: Tor Boacciana
places.address: Via del Ponte di Tor Boacciana, Roma RM
places.summary: A medieval tower standing on Roman ruins on the bank of the Tiber, about four kilometres from the river mouth, at the edge of Roma Capitale's territory with the comune di Fiumicino. The quartiere's own article names it among its military structures. it.wikipedia records that it is managed by the Parco archeologico di Ostia antica. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.
places.history: The base of the tower is made of ruins of imperial Roman date, probably what remains of a lighthouse or a watchtower of the 2nd century, dated by the stamps on its brick and plausibly tied to the commerce of Porto. The tower above it is of about the twelfth century, and is identified with the solitary tower that Richard the Lionheart described. The Bovazzani family owned it, which is probably the source of the name. It was restored in 1406 under Innocent VII and in 1420 under Martin V, and served as the papal customs post from 1562 until 1568, when the customs moved to Tor San Michele. The Roman remains beneath the tower sometimes carry a separate entry as a faro romano; they are the same object and are treated here as one place.

places.name: Idroscalo di Ostia
places.summary: The site of the former Idroscalo Lido di Roma Carlo Del Prete, a seaplane base at the mouth of the Tiber, reached from via dell'Idroscalo. Nothing of the base is in service: the marina, the LIPU oasis and the literary park now occupy the ground. Turismo Roma records that the landscape here is still marked by the bilancioni, the lift nets used for eel fishing.
places.history: The base was built to the design of the engineer Raffaele Tarantini and opened in 1919. Erosion forced its dismantling in 1922, and it was re-established a little further along from 3 March 1926; after 1928 it carried the name of the aviator Carlo Del Prete. Francesco de Pinedo's Two Americas cruise ended here in 1927, and Italo Balbo's Decennale squadron arrived on 12 August 1933; the base housed the Societa Aerea Mediterranea and Ala Littoria. In 1929 the futurist painter Gerardo Dottori decorated the walls of the waiting room, of which a sketch survives. German forces destroyed the main structures in 1943. From the 1960s Roman fishermen built a spontaneous settlement on the site, and about 35 dwellings were cleared in 2010. Pier Paolo Pasolini's body was found in this area on 2 November 1975. it.wikipedia records that the settlement inspired Federico Fellini, Nanni Moretti, Claudio Caligari and Pier Paolo Pasolini.

places.name: Porto Turistico di Roma
places.address: Lungomare Duca degli Abruzzi 84, 00121 Roma RM
places.summary: The marina immediately south of the mouth of the Tiber, with a vehicle entrance from via del Porto di Roma. The operator gives 840 berths, 100 shops and restaurants and 1400 car spaces, and a promenade of a kilometre; it.wikipedia instead gives 833 berths, 80 shops, 1200 metres of promenade, over 10,000 square metres of exhibition space, an open-air amphitheatre of 750 seats and a 400-tonne travel lift. The berths take vessels from 8 to 60 metres. The operator states that boats up to 20 metres staying at most two nights need no booking and should call the control tower on VHF channel 74, which is worked from 07.00 to 23.00; the office is open 09.00 to 13.00 and 15.00 to 19.00. The marina also holds the Mario Pastore visitor centre of the LIPU oasis and, for now, the Biblioteca Elsa Morante.
places.history: it.wikipedia records that the marina was designed in the 1990s as part of the regeneration of the Idroscalo area, alongside the LIPU oasis; that works began in 1998; that it was built by ATI S.p.A.; and that it cost about 120 billion lire. It opened in 2001.

places.name: Centro Habitat Mediterraneo
places.address: Via dell'Idroscalo, 00121 Lido di Ostia RM
places.summary: A nature reserve run by LIPU on the site of the former seaplane base, built around a reconstructed coastal wetland. LIPU's own figures give the site as 20 hectares, instituted in 2001, with 219 bird species recorded. A nature trail reaches three large wooden hides and structures for wildlife photography; there is an open-air classroom, and the Mario Pastore visitor centre is a wooden chalet in the car park of the Porto Turistico. The Porto Turistico's own page adds three modern Skua hides and a butterfly garden. Purple heron breeds here. LIPU states that the visitor centre opens on Mondays, Wednesdays, Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays from 10.00 to 13.00 for information and for wildlife rescue; that on Saturdays and Sundays from 10.00 to 13.00 there is free access to the oasis; and that guided visits can be booked on any day of the week.
places.history: LIPU records that the centre was made on the ground of a former open-air dump, on the site where Pier Paolo Pasolini was killed. The Porto Turistico's page describes the same ground as a naturalistic centre of more than 20 hectares laid out where an open-air dump had been, created alongside the marina in the regeneration of the Idroscalo area.

places.name: Parco Letterario Pier Paolo Pasolini
places.summary: A garden on via dell'Idroscalo, on the place where Pier Paolo Pasolini was killed; his body was found in this area on 2 November 1975. LIPU and the Porto Turistico both record that the ground was recovered and laid out as a literary garden and that it is now instituted as the Parco Letterario Pier Paolo Pasolini. A memorial to Pasolini stands on via dell'Idroscalo. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.
places.history: The park adjoins the Centro Habitat Mediterraneo, on the ground of the former seaplane base and of the settlement that grew there from the 1960s.

places.name: Ex Colonia marina Vittorio Emanuele III
places.summary: A seaside children's colony of about 16,000 square metres, occupying the block bounded by lungomare Paolo Toscanelli, via Adolfo Cozza, largo delle Sirene and via Giuliano da Sangallo, with a second address at via Adolfo Cozza 7. It is built as two linked sections: the eastern one is four comb-plan buildings on a hospital model, the western one is arranged around a courtyard. An underpass was built so that the children could reach the sand directly, and Roma Capitale records that it still exists. it.wikipedia gives the present uses of the complex as a Caritas soup kitchen, a seniors' centre, the technical office of Municipio X, a chapel, a hostel, the Biblioteca Elsa Morante and the Teatro del Lido; Roma Capitale's own sheet names a soup kitchen, a seniors' centre and temporary housing for people in need.
places.history: A colonia marina was built here in 1916 to Marcello Piacentini's design, in reinforced concrete, with refectories, kitchens, day rooms and two large dormitories holding 80 beds in all. In 1925 the Governatorato's plan against tuberculosis proposed enlarging it, and the extension was entrusted to Vincenzo Fasolo, whose works began on 20 January 1927. The building was inaugurated on 24 January 1932 in the presence of Queen Elena, and named for Vittorio Emanuele III because the year fell in the twenty-fifth of his reign; its official name was the Ospizio Marino e Colonia di Profilassi. A chapel of 1932, also by Fasolo, belongs to the complex. German forces occupied and half destroyed it in 1943 and it stood idle until it was restored in the early 1950s; it worked as a colonia until 1983. The complex appears in Tinto Brass's film Snack Bar Budapest of 1988.

places.name: Teatro del Lido di Ostia
places.summary: A municipal theatre inside the ex Colonia marina complex, and one of the four venues in Roma Capitale's Teatri in Comune circuit, with the Teatro Biblioteca Quarticciolo, the Teatro Tor Bella Monaca and the Teatro Villa Pamphilj. Its season is published through Teatri in Comune rather than as a standing timetable.
places.history: It is a teatro di cintura, a category defined by the Legge regionale 15 settembre 2005 n. 16 for theatres in the outer districts of a city. it.wikipedia records that local artists started the theatre in 1997, that restoration began in 2000, that the new venue was inaugurated in February 2003, that it closed in June 2008, and that on 26 February 2010 a committee reoccupied it, after which it reopened under an agreement.

places.name: Biblioteca Elsa Morante
places.address: Lungomare Duca degli Abruzzi 84, 00121 Roma RM
places.summary: A public library of Roma Capitale, normally housed in the ex Colonia marina and at present working from a substitute address inside the Porto Turistico di Roma, which Biblioteche di Roma prints as Porto Turistico di Roma, Lungomare Duca degli Abruzzi 84, 00121 Roma, telephone 06 45460481. Biblioteche di Roma gives hours for 2 January to 31 December 2026 of Monday to Friday 09.00 to 19.00 and Saturday 09.00 to 13.00, closed on Sundays. Most of the collection is on open shelves, but the Fondo Ostia, which holds material on the history and on the natural and urban landscape of the Roman coast, and the professional bibliography are not, and have to be asked for at the desk. There is a study room of 24 places. Its SBN codes are RMBO2 and RM0632.
places.history: The library opened in 2001 with funds from the Giubileo 2000 and belongs to Roma Capitale's Istituzione Sistema Biblioteche e Centri Culturali. Biblioteche di Roma's open data on holdings by type of document gives about 31,000 books, 3,100 DVDs and 2,500 audio CDs; it.wikipedia gives the holding at the temporary site as about 7,000 volumes, and dates the move to 4 September 2025, made for energy-efficiency works. it.wikipedia and the library's OPAC also record a collection of nearly a hundred titles in Comunicazione Aumentativa e Alternativa. The library is named for the writer Elsa Morante.

places.name: Ufficio postale di Ostia Lido
places.summary: The post office building on piazzale della Posta, at the corner of via Ostiense and corso Duca di Genova. A colonnaded portico rises off a travertine stair, the brick-clad colonnade carrying a circular travertine canopy around an open basin; the structure is reinforced concrete faced in fair-face brick alternating with travertine slabs, the interiors are tiled in light green, dark green, grey and blue, the caretaker's flat is painted in an orange called Arsonia, and the doors, windows and fittings are copper and anticorodal. In the basin stands a fountain in repousse copper by Napoleone Martinuzzi, 1892 to 1977, a Murano-born glass artist and sculptor, with the basin lined in blue Murano glass brick; it.wikipedia describes the figures as two double-tailed sirens holding cups of water above their heads, while ArchiDiAP, the source it.wikipedia cites, calls them two muses. The building still houses the Roma Ostia Lido post office, frazionario 55472. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.
places.history: Angiolo Mazzoni designed the building for the Ministero delle comunicazioni and it was inaugurated in 1934; ArchiDiAP independently dates the work to 1934. Mazzoni was chief engineer of the Ferrovie dello Stato and designed the post offices of Grosseto, Sabaudia, Littoria, now Latina, Palermo, La Spezia, Trento and Ostia. He co-signed the Manifesto futurista dell'architettura aerea with Filippo Tommaso Marinetti and joined the board of the review Futurismo-Sant'Elia, and both ArchiDiAP and it.wikipedia record that Marinetti visited the building at different times of day to watch the light in the portico. Martinuzzi also worked with Mazzoni on the post offices of Palermo and Gorizia and on Venice station. The office was originally the Ricevitoria Postelegrafonica di Ostia Lido, and it.wikipedia records that the 1934 plaque reading REGIE POSTE TELEGRAFI TELEFONI is still at the entrance.

places.name: Cineland
places.summary: A multiplex cinema and leisure complex inside the shell of the Meccanica Romana factory, its neobaroque facade turned toward the via del Mare: two transverse blocks joined by a central one. It has 14 screens and 2,860 seats, 16 bowling lanes, an arcade and a virtual-reality centre, restaurants and shops, 3,000 parking spaces and 60,000 square metres of green. Roma Capitale gives the covered area as 15,000 square metres; it.wikipedia's infobox gives 14,000 square metres of walkable floor area. Its programme and ticketing are published on its own site.
places.history: The factory was built between 1927 and 1929 to a design by Pietro Barbieri and opened in 1929 as S.T.I.M.A., Societa Trattori Italiani e Macchine Agricole Italia, a name proposed by Mussolini; it.wikipedia says it was built at the wish of the engineer Pio Perrone, while Roma Capitale's sheet says at Mussolini's. It was meant to seed an industrial district served by the Roma-Ostia Lido railway of 1924, and was left isolated when that did not follow. It became the Societa Acciaierie Romane in 1941, was bought by Breda Meccanica Romana in 1952 to build machinery and spare parts for the Roma-Lido trains, and closed in 1973. The conversion was designed by Maria Guarrera and Bruno Spinozzi to a project dated 10 December 1987 and opened on 15 September 1999 by Ci.Me. Grandi Impianti S.r.l. of Giuseppe Ciotoli and Giuseppe Merluzzi, at a cost of 26 billion lire. All the original facades were kept and consolidated by light-impact methods, the steel frame was reproduced, the plaster was hacked off and remade, and the pilasters and capitals were restored.

places.name: Palazzo dell'ex GIL
places.address: Corso Duca di Genova 82, Roma RM
places.summary: A 1930s block on corso Duca di Genova, with a second frontage at via delle Sirene 79, built as the local seat of the Opera Nazionale Balilla. Three ranges stand in an L around a rectangular courtyard inside a perimeter wall measuring 120 by 70 metres, and a semicircular three-storey tower rises to 18.5 metres over an open ground-floor portico. A 1930s decorative panel by Oddo Aliventi survives in the meeting room. It has stood empty since the school closed in 2009.
places.history: Paolo Benadusi designed it and it was built between 1933 and 1936, inaugurated on 8 August 1935 in Mussolini's presence. It later held a public school, which closed in July 2009 because the building was unfit for use. The Region transferred it to Roma Capitale in 2020 and Roma Capitale to Municipio X, which plans to restore it as the seat of the X Mare group of the local police and as an office of the giudice di pace.

places.name: Scuola Fratelli Garrone
places.address: Corso Duca di Genova, Roma RM
places.summary: A school building of 1934 to 1935 on corso Duca di Genova, laid out in three ranges for three streams of teaching: 24 elementary classrooms, ten rooms for the ginnasio and ten for vocational teaching. The elementary block has a large refectory and three special-subject rooms; the gymnasium has changing rooms, showers and its own entrance; the first-aid post also has an independent entrance so that it could be used outside school hours and on days when the school was shut. It is a working primary school, a secondary site of the Istituto Comprensivo Via Giuliano da Sangallo, and no public access is published for it; it is a building to look at from the street.
places.history: The Governatorato di Roma commissioned the school from Ignazio Guidi in 1934; it was built in 1934 and 1935 and opened in 1935, dedicated to the brothers Giuseppe and Eugenio Garrone, both of whom held the gold medal for military valour. Guidi designed it so that the partitions could later be moved and the building converted to a single kind of teaching. It was described in Capitolium. Rassegna mensile del Governatorato, anno X n. 8, 1934, under the title Una nuova scuola al Lido di Roma.

places.name: Chiesa di Santa Monica
places.address: Piazza di Santa Monica, Roma RM
places.summary: A parish church on piazza di Santa Monica, built to a Latin-cross plan with a reinforced-concrete structure, the crossing marked by the intersection of the four main beams that carry the ceiling, and a portico linking the church to the rest of the parish complex. It is dedicated to Monica of Tagaste, who died at Ostia. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.
places.history: The parish began as a vicecura in January 1956 and was erected as a parish on 13 November 1958 by the decree Romanus Pontifex of the Cardinal Vicar Clemente Micara. Work on the church began on 13 June 1968, the feast of Corpus Domini, with Paul VI present to bless the foundation stone; Ernesto Vichi designed it. It was opened on the evening of 7 December 1972 by Remigio Ragonesi, auxiliary bishop of Rome, and consecrated on 22 December 1973. John Paul II visited the parish on 8 May 1983, and Francis on 3 June 2018, for the Corpus Domini mass at Ostia.

places.name: Parco Willy Ferrero
places.summary: A public garden between piazzale Lorenzo Gaspari and lungomare Duca degli Abruzzi. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.
places.history: No source states a history of the garden beyond its name and its position, which the quartiere's own article records.

entries.name: Tor San Michele
entries.note: An octagonal casemated fort begun in 1559 after the Tiber flood of 1557, on a design attributed to Michelangelo; its own article records that it can be visited by booking.

entries.name: Tor Boacciana
entries.note: A twelfth-century tower on the Tiber bank standing on the remains of what was probably a Roman lighthouse of the 2nd century, and the papal customs post from 1562 to 1568.

entries.name: Idroscalo di Ostia
entries.note: The ground of the seaplane base opened in 1919 and destroyed by German forces in 1943, where Italo Balbo's Decennale squadron landed on 12 August 1933.

entries.name: Parco Letterario Pier Paolo Pasolini
entries.note: A garden on via dell'Idroscalo laid out on the place where Pasolini was killed; his body was found in this area on 2 November 1975.

entries.name: Centro Habitat Mediterraneo
entries.note: LIPU's 20-hectare reserve around a reconstructed coastal wetland, with 219 bird species recorded; free access on Saturdays and Sundays from 10.00 to 13.00.

entries.name: Porto Turistico di Roma
entries.note: The marina south of the river mouth, opened in 2001, with 840 berths taking vessels from 8 to 60 metres and a control tower working VHF 74 from 07.00 to 23.00.

entries.name: Ex Colonia marina Vittorio Emanuele III
entries.note: A children's seaside colony of about 16,000 square metres, begun in 1916 by Marcello Piacentini and extended by Vincenzo Fasolo, inaugurated on 24 January 1932.

entries.name: Teatro del Lido di Ostia
entries.note: A municipal theatre inside the ex Colonia marina block, one of the four venues in Roma Capitale's Teatri in Comune circuit, which publishes its season.

entries.name: Biblioteca Elsa Morante
entries.note: Working from the Porto Turistico while its own building has works done; ask at the desk for the Fondo Ostia, on the history and landscape of the Roman coast.

entries.name: Ufficio postale di Ostia Lido
entries.note: Angiolo Mazzoni's post office of 1934, its portico set around an open basin holding a repousse copper fountain by Napoleone Martinuzzi lined with blue Murano glass brick.

entries.name: Cineland
entries.note: Fourteen screens and 2,860 seats, plus 16 bowling lanes, inside the shell of a tractor factory of 1927 to 1929; the conversion opened on 15 September 1999.

entries.name: Palazzo dell'ex GIL
entries.note: Paolo Benadusi's block of 1933 to 1936 for the Opera Nazionale Balilla, with a semicircular tower 18.5 metres high; it has stood empty since the school closed in 2009.

entries.name: Chiesa di Santa Monica
entries.note: Paul VI blessed the foundation stone on 13 June 1968; the church opened on 7 December 1972, and Francis came for the Corpus Domini mass at Ostia on 3 June 2018.
